audit.whatIsWrong: The two available win-rate sources disagree by more than seventeen points. MC_WR_TABLES.sejuani.kayle is 48.11 over 291 games; the packet says 65.22 over 69 games. The page is built as EVEN at 7/10, which fits the 48 reading and flatly contradicts the 65 reading.
audit.why: 48% and 65% describe two different matchups. At 65 this is one of Sejuani's best lanes and the level chart should lean heavily her way; at 48 the current chart is roughly right. I cannot pick between the sources from the data I have, so I changed no rating, no difficulty and no stage side, and raised it as a question instead of guessing.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side give Kayle levels 1-3, but whys[0], whys[1] and whys[2] all describe those stages as neutral: 'neither can force a decisive trade', 'neither side can safely commit', 'neither scores a kill'. spikes[0] then calls level 3 Sejuani's window outright. Levels 4-5 are scored Kayle while whys[3] says 'Sejuani controls this window' and spikes[1] describes Kayle's autos barely denting her.
audit.why: Four stage captions argue against their own sides. Kayle is melee with no dash before her passive grants range, and Sejuani's level-3 Q-W-E chain lands on a champion with no mobility to break it — the prose is right and the sides are stale. I have not applied the fix because the correct chart depends on which win rate is real, and re-siding four stages on the strength of a disputed 48-versus-65 split is exactly the guess the brief forbids.
audit.corrected: Nothing applied. Levels 1-3 and 4-5 need re-siding once the win-rate source is settled; flagged in questionsForUser.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3], spikes[1], early and mid all rest the matchup on Sejuani's resistances absorbing Kayle's poke, and none of them mention Radiant Blast. Riot's text: 'Kayle conjures a portal, summoning a celestial sword that pierces through enemies, slowing, damaging, and reducing the resistances of all hit.' Her Q shreds the exact stat those four fields say protects Sejuani, and it is also a slow, which Frost Armor makes her immune to.
audit.why: This is the interaction the whole page is built around and it was never stated. Telling a Sejuani her armour absorbs Kayle's harassment, while omitting that Kayle's 900-range Q on a 12-second cooldown removes that armour, gives her a plan Kayle deletes with one button. The other half is free value in the other direction: Radiant Blast is Kayle's only slow, and Fury of the North grants 'immunity to slows' while Frost Armor holds, so the shred lands but the kiting does not.
audit.corrected: Radiant Blast's resistance shred is now stated in whys[3], spikes[1] and mid, with its 12-second rank-1 cooldown as the window to step up. The slow immunity is in early and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] says Kayle chunks 'a meaningful fraction of Sejuani's max HP through Silver Bolts-style percent damage' and late says she has 'percent-current-HP on-hit damage from Starfire Spellblade'. Riot's Starfire Spellblade text: 'Kayle's next attack smites her target with celestial fire, dealing bonus damage proportionate to their missing health.'
audit.why: Wrong on both counts and the error inverts the advice. Missing health is not current health and not max health, and Silver Bolts is Vayne's ability, not Kayle's. Scaling on missing health means Starfire Spellblade is weakest against a healthy Sejuani and strongest as she drops — so a big HP pool is a defence against it, not the liability the page describes, and the real rule is to disengage before the execute range rather than to fear the first hit.
audit.corrected: whys[5] and late now describe missing-health scaling and drop the Silver Bolts reference.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2], mid, winCon, loading and breakdown.cooldowns all key the plan to Divine Judgment's 'long cooldown' being spent, without ever giving the number.
audit.why: Divine Judgment is 160 seconds at rank 1, falling to 120 and then 80. A hundred and sixty seconds is not merely 'long' — it is more than two minutes in which Kayle has no answer to a landed Glacial Prison, and it is the single most actionable number on this page. Radiant Blast at 12 seconds and Celestial Blessing at a flat 15 are the other two clocks worth naming.
audit.corrected: 160s at rank 1 stated in wants.you[2], mid, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and loading; Radiant Blast's 12s in whys[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal timing, despite Celestial Blessing being a flat-15-second heal.
audit.why: Riot: 'Kayle heals and grants Move Speed to herself and the nearest ally.' On a 15-second cooldown at every rank it recurs inside the extended trades this page tells Sejuani to seek, and Grievous Wounds is what makes the chip stick.

edits.before: Kayle is one of the weakest level-1 champions in the game — no ranged form yet, low base stats, and every auto applies your Frost stacks passively, so do not waste Q trying to chase. Walk up, absorb her auto-attacks through Permafrost's bonus resistances, and let your passive armor build for free. At level 2 you can threaten a Q knockup to interrupt her Starfire Spellblade farming pattern, but her kit has no CC to answer yours — she just tries to walk backward. Level 3 is the first real window: Q in to knock her up, both hits of Winter's Wrath to stack Frost, then Permafrost stun before she can step out. She has no dash, no escape, and her pre-6 form is a melee champion with a slow attack animation — this is the window to punish any greed.
edits.after: Kayle is one of the weakest level-1 champions in the game — no ranged form yet, low base stats — so do not waste Q trying to chase. Walk up, absorb her autos while Fury of the North builds Frost Armor for free, and remember that armour comes from the passive, not from Permafrost. At level 2 you can threaten a Q knockup to interrupt her Starfire Spellblade farming, and she has no CC to answer yours; she just walks backward. Radiant Blast is her only slow, and Frost Armor makes you immune to slows while it holds, so it does not stop your walk-up. Level 3 is the first real window: Q in to knock her up, both hits of Winter's Wrath to stack Frost, then Permafrost before she steps out. No dash, no escape — punish any greed.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely neutral — Kayle's passive grants her longer auto range and she starts poking more freely, but her damage still cannot chunk through your Permafrost resistances before your W cools down and you stack Frost again. Respect the range, hug the wave for minion body cover, and farm. Level 6 shifts the matchup in your favor for a window: Glacial Prison is a skill-shot that Kayle has no dash to dodge, and it creates a blizzard that keeps stunning if she stands inside. She has Divine Judgment to survive one all-in, so your job is to fake the engage, bait the R invulnerability, then immediately recast Glacial Prison when the blizzard lands and chain the E stun — if her R is burned you finish the trade.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely neutral — her passive lengthens her auto range and she pokes more freely, but she cannot chunk through Frost Armor before W cools down and you re-stack. The one thing that changes that is Radiant Blast: it pierces at 900 range and reduces the resistances of everyone hit, so her real pattern is shred first, then auto. Step up on its 12-second downtime, hug the wave for minion cover, and farm. Level 6 shifts the lane your way for a window: Glacial Prison is a skillshot Kayle has no dash to dodge. She has Divine Judgment to survive one all-in, so fake the engage, bait the invulnerability, and go the moment it is spent — at rank 1 that buys you 160 seconds.

edits.before: Once Kayle completes her first major item she transitions into a ranged hypercarry with percent-current-HP on-hit damage from Starfire Spellblade that punishes your massive HP pool, and your armor stacking cannot keep up. Never solo her at this stage — your role is to R her in a teamfight, eat the Divine Judgment, and let your carries follow through. Save Glacial Prison for multi-man catches; a single-target Kayle stun that she R's out of is a wasted teamfight button. Your lane advantage from levels 3-5 should have bought enough pressure to control Dragon and plates — convert that into a team lead so the game does not reach the window where she hits her third item.
edits.after: Once Kayle finishes her first major item she becomes a ranged hypercarry, and Starfire Spellblade's bonus damage scales with your missing health — so every exchange gets worse the longer you stay in it, and disengaging early matters more than stacking another armour item. Never solo her at this stage; your role is to R her in a teamfight, eat the Divine Judgment, and let your carries follow through. Save Glacial Prison for multi-man catches — a single-target stun she ults out of is a wasted teamfight button. Convert the pressure you built at levels 3-5 into Dragon and plates so the game never reaches her third item.

notes: Win-rate sources conflict badly here: MC_WR_TABLES says 48.11 over 291 games, the packet says 65.22 over 69. Because the whole stage chart hangs on which is true, I made no rating, difficulty or side changes and every edit below is a pure ability-interaction or cooldown correction that holds either way. Point 3 documents four stage captions that already contradict their sides and should be re-sided once the source is settled. One thing I could not verify and therefore did not put on the page: whether a target under Divine Judgment can still be stunned by Permafrost. Riot's text says only 'makes an ally invulnerable', and sejuani.json's needsResearch is empty, which the brief defines as unknown rather than no. If CC does apply through it, the correct advice in mid changes from 'bait the invulnerability' to 'stun through it and hold the damage', which is a materially different play. The 'Permafrost resistances' mislabel for Fury of the North survives in whys[6] and spikes[2], which I had no separate reason to open.
